model.notes: The take rules target the main group of rejected winners: JCT, PIEVERSE, MAGMA and SHELL shorts where retail had collapsed short while top traders stayed long. The current take rule using the 1h cap is retained unchanged as an anchor. Two variants are added alongside it: one that replaces the 1h cap with a 4h cap, and one based on the retail-versus-top-trader divergence. The skip rules add a capitulation-bounce filter and a lower-threshold momentum filter for 20x+ shorts. The proposed long skip rules already show strong results, so no new long rules were added.

new.why: Short into a small up-hour where the crowd has shifted short-to-long already (shorts squeezed out) but aggressive buying is not dominant: the bounce is exhausting, entering higher improves the price.

Price ticks up while open interest drops: a short-covering pop, not new longs. Once covering ends there is no fuel left, so entering on the pop gives a better short price with lower further adverse excursion.

The coin has already moved against the signal but activity and bursts are fading: buying exhaustion after the run-up. Entering after it means part of the adverse excursion is already behind, so a 5% stop survives more often.

Funding turned positive with fresh longs piling in on an up-hour: longs are crowded and paying. This is the late-long state that tends to unwind, so the short entered here should see small adverse excursion and allow a 3% stop.

patterns.notes: Close rules have historically lost on average (book exits mostly by timeout with positive drift), so only narrow early-hour breakout closes are proposed. Short stops (1-2%) cut 70-84% of winners; no state found that reliably shrinks adverse excursion, so the entry rules aim at entering after an exhausted bounce, with stops of 3-5% at most.
